newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-Salinas aide denies role in Colosio murder.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Salinas aide denies role in Colosio murder.

text.p: A top aide to former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari on Wednesday denounced as "irresponsible" insinuations that he was involved in the assassination of former presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio.

Jose Cordoba Montoya, who was chief of staff under Salinas until a few days after Colosio was shot, appeared voluntarily for three hours before leftist congressmen on a special commission investigating the assassination.

Cordoba, who recently testified before the government's special prosecutor in the case, vehemently denied any role in the Colosio murder, adding that he would sue two legislators on the panel for damages after they implied his involvement.
He said his suit also would name Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, former presidential candidate of the leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD), for making similar statements.

Colosio, who almost certainly would have become president, was gunned down at a March 1994 campaign event in the northern border city Tijuana in Mexico's worst political assassination in half a century. One man is in jail for pulling the trigger.
